closed_issues.title: chore(backend): migrate to Spring Boot 4.1 and bump all backend dependencies
closed_issues.author: criew
closed_issues.body:
## Summary

Upgrade the OPAA backend to Spring Boot 4.1 and bring every other backend dependency to its latest stable release. This is a coordinated bump of the Spring Boot / Spring AI baseline plus all supporting libraries and the Gradle wrapper, executed in a single feature branch.

## Motivation

- Keep the platform on a fresh, supported baseline; Spring Boot 3.5.x support will wind down and 4.x is now the active line (4.0 GA in 2025-11, 4.1 GA in 2026-06).
- Spring Boot 4 is a prerequisite for Spring AI 2.0 (2026-06 GA); the current Spring AI 1.1.x is not SB4-compatible.
- Align on the Jakarta EE 11 / Servlet 6.1 / Spring Framework 7 stack now that Java 21 is our baseline.
- Pick up the JSpecify null-safety work in Spring, the Jackson 3 default, and the improved Actuator/DevTools defaults.
- Reduce carrying cost by bumping the long tail (Spotless, OpenAPI Generator, JJWT, Caffeine, Awaitility, Gradle wrapper) in the same pass.

## Scope

Backend-only dependency and tooling bumps. All version changes go through `backend/gradle/libs.versions.toml` per the repository dependency-management rules.

| Library / Tool | Current | Target |
|---|---|---|
| Spring Boot | 3.5.10 | 4.1.x (latest patch of 4.1) |
| Spring AI | 1.1.2 | 2.0.x (latest patch of 2.0) |
| Spring Dependency Management plugin | 1.1.7 | 1.1.7 (verify SB4 compatibility; keep unless a blocker) |
| Spotless | 8.2.1 | 8.9.0 |
| OpenAPI Generator | 7.20.0 | 7.23.0 (or 7.24.0 if released; keep `useSpringBoot3=true` semantics working under SB4) |
| JJWT | 0.12.6 | 0.13.0 |
| Caffeine | 3.2.0 | 3.2.4 |
| Awaitility | 4.3.0 | Latest patch pulled via SB4 BOM |
| Liquibase Core | via SB3.5 BOM (4.x) | Whatever the SB4 BOM ships (currently 5.x); confirm changelog compatibility |
| Testcontainers | via SB3.5 BOM (1.x) | Whatever the SB4 BOM ships (currently 2.x); regenerate/validate integration tests |
| Gradle Wrapper | 9.3.1 | 9.6 |
| Java baseline | 21 | 21 (no change required) |

## Out of Scope

- Frontend dependency bumps — tracked in a separate issue.
- Product/feature behavior changes; this is a pure infrastructure/chore bump.
- Removing or replacing the `spring-dependency-management` plugin with Gradle's native BOM import — evaluate but do not execute here.
- Migrating to a Jackson-3-only stack when a Jackson-2 compatibility shim (`spring-boot-jackson2`) already unblocks us; only remove Jackson 2 usages that are directly touched.
- GraalVM native-image (would require Java 25+); note but do not adopt.

## Migration Steps

1. **Land on latest 3.5.x first.** Bump to the freshest Spring Boot 3.5 patch, run `./gradlew build test`, and clean up any deprecation warnings that block a clean SB4 upgrade.
2. **Wire in the `spring-boot-properties-migrator`** dependency for the first SB4 boot to surface renamed `application.yml` properties.
3. **Upgrade the platform.** Bump `spring-boot`, `spring-boot-dependencies`, and the Spring Boot Gradle plugin to 4.1.x. Confirm Spring Framework 7 + Jakarta EE 11 assumptions in our code (Servlet 6.1 signatures, no `javax.*` leftovers).
4. **Jackson 3 alignment.** Replace usages of `@JsonComponent` → `@JacksonComponent`, `@JsonMixin` → `@JacksonMixin`, `JsonObjectSerializer` → `ObjectValueSerializer`, `Jackson2ObjectMapperBuilderCustomizer` → `JsonMapperBuilderCustomizer`; move `ObjectMapper` bean expectations to `JsonMapper` / `XmlMapper` where applicable. Where a rewrite is disproportionate, keep the deprecated Jackson-2 module (`spring-boot-jackson2`) explicitly and document why.
5. **Spring AI 2.0 migration.** Bump `spring-ai` to 2.0.x, adjust to the JSpecify null-safety annotations and any renamed helpers referenced in the Spring AI 2.0 release notes.
6. **Property renames.** Apply the SB4 property-rename table (e.g. `spring.jackson.read/write.*` → `spring.jackson.json.read/write.*`, `spring.data.mongodb.*` → `spring.mongodb.*`, `spring.dao.exceptiontranslation.enabled` → `spring.persistence.exceptiontranslation.enabled`, `spring.session.redis.*` → `spring.session.data.redis.*`, `spring.kafka.retry.topic.backoff.random` → `spring.kafka.retry.topic.backoff.jitter`). Cross-check with the properties-migrator output.
7. **Package/type moves.** Update imports: `BootstrapRegistry` (moved to `org.springframework.boot.bootstrap`), `EnvironmentPostProcessor` (moved to `org.springframework.boot`), test-only `@PropertyMapping` (moved to `org.springframework.boot.test.context`).
8. **Actuator nullability.** Replace `org.springframework.lang.Nullable` with `org.jspecify.annotations.Nullable` in Actuator-touching code.
9. **Auto-config sanity check.** We do not use Undertow, Pulsar Reactive, Spring Session Hazelcast/MongoDB, or Spring Batch, but confirm nothing in our build depends on them. Verify DevTools live-reload (now off by default) and Health Probes (now on by default) still match our expectations.
10. **Adjacent bumps.** Bump Spotless (8.9.0), OpenAPI Generator (7.23.0), JJWT (0.13.0), Caffeine (3.2.4), and re-run generation for OpenAPI DTOs; confirm the generator's Spring template still emits code that compiles against SB4 (esp. `useSpringBoot3` flag semantics).
11. **Gradle wrapper.** `./gradlew wrapper --gradle-version 9.6 --distribution-type all` and commit both `gradle-wrapper.properties` and `gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.jar`.
12. **Verify.** `./gradlew clean spotlessCheck build test` green; `./gradlew bootRun` boots against the local Docker Compose stack; Actuator health endpoint responds; OpenAPI-generated DTOs still round-trip via the frontend contract.

## Breaking Changes to Watch

Sourced from the official Spring Boot 4.0 Migration Guide and 4.0 / 4.1 release notes:

1. **Jackson 3 becomes the default** (group id `tools.jackson`). Renamed annotations and helpers (`@JsonComponent` → `@JacksonComponent`, `@JsonMixin` → `@JacksonMixin`, `JsonObjectSerializer` → `ObjectValueSerializer`, `Jackson2ObjectMapperBuilderCustomizer` → `JsonMapperBuilderCustomizer`); prefer `JsonMapper`/`XmlMapper` beans. Jackson-2 compatibility available via the deprecated `spring-boot-jackson2` module.
2. **Configuration property renames** — see step 6 above.
3. **Package/type moves** — see step 7 above.
4. **Auto-configuration removals**: Undertow (not Servlet-6.1-compatible), Pulsar Reactive, Spring Session Hazelcast/MongoDB, Spock integration. DevTools live-reload defaults to off; Actuator health probes (liveness/readiness) default to on.
5. **Actuator nullability annotations** switched from Spring's `Nullable` to JSpecify `Nullable`.
6. **Spring Data changes**: Elasticsearch `RestClient` → `Rest5Client` (`Rest5ClientBuilderCustomizer`); MongoDB UUID/BigDecimal representation now requires explicit configuration.
7. **Spring Batch** runs in-memory by default; DB-backed storage needs the new `spring-boot-starter-batch-jdbc`.
8. **Removed from dependency management**: Spring Retry (moved to Spring Framework), classic uber-jar loader, embedded exec launch scripts, Undertow.

Additional watch items:

- Spring AI 2.0 targets Spring Framework 7 / SB4 / Jackson 3 / JSpecify — 1.1.x has no forward-compat guarantee (see the compat discussion linked below).
- OpenAPI Generator 7.23+ contains breaking changes with fallback flags; re-check the generated DTO diff.
- Liquibase 5.x and Testcontainers 2.x are major bumps managed via the SB4 BOM — read their changelogs before merging.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All backend versions in `backend/gradle/libs.versions.toml` updated per the Scope table (or with a documented reason if a target release regresses).
- [ ] `./gradlew clean spotlessCheck build test` passes locally.
- [ ] `./gradlew bootRun` starts against the local Docker Compose stack; `/actuator/health` returns 200.
- [ ] All SB4 property renames applied (or explicitly acknowledged via the `spring-boot-properties-migrator` output) in every `application*.yml`.
- [ ] Jackson usages migrated to the SB4/Jackson 3 idioms (or explicitly kept on the `spring-boot-jackson2` shim with a code comment).
- [ ] Gradle wrapper on 9.6, wrapper jar committed.
- [ ] `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, and `docs/decisions/0002-mvp-technology-stack.md` version references updated to match the new baseline.
- [ ] Documentation updated (standing criterion for architectural changes) — release-notes-style summary in the PR body plus a follow-up ADR draft if any structural decision emerged (e.g. Jackson 3 adoption strategy, whether to keep the dependency-management plugin).

## Dependencies

None. Can start as soon as it is prioritized. Recommendation: merge this before the frontend bump issue so the two migrations do not overlap in CI red time.

## References

- Spring Boot 4.0 Release Notes: https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/wiki/Spring-Boot-4.0-Release-Notes
- Spring Boot 4.1 Release Notes: https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/wiki/Spring-Boot-4.1-Release-Notes
- Spring Boot 4.0 Migration Guide: https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/wiki/Spring-Boot-4.0-Migration-Guide
- Spring Boot 4.0 GA announcement: https://spring.io/blog/2025/11/20/spring-boot-4-0-0-available-now/
- Spring Boot 4.1 GA announcement: https://spring.io/blog/2026/06/10/spring-boot-4/
- Spring AI 2.0 GA announcement: https://spring.io/blog/2026/06/12/spring-ai-2-0-0-GA-available-now/
- Spring AI Boot 4 compatibility discussion: https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-ai/discussions/5149
- Spring Boot dependency management plugin docs: https://docs.spring.io/spring-boot/gradle-plugin/managing-dependencies.html
- Spotless changelog: https://github.com/diffplug/spotless/blob/main/plugin-gradle/CHANGES.md
- OpenAPI Generator releases: https://github.com/OpenAPITools/openapi-generator/releases
- Liquibase releases: https://github.com/liquibase/liquibase/releases
- Testcontainers Java releases: https://github.com/testcontainers/testcontainers-java/releases
- JJWT changelog: https://github.com/jwtk/jjwt/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
- Caffeine: https://github.com/ben-manes/caffeine

## Technical Notes

- Java 21 is already at or above the SB4 baseline (SB4 requires 17+); no JDK bump needed for the runtime.
- Gradle 9.3.1 is above the SB4 minimum (8.14+); bump to 9.6 is quality-of-life, not required.
- GraalVM native-image support would require Java 25+ — out of scope, but worth capturing as a future consideration.
- The Spring Dependency Management plugin is still compatible with SB4 for now. If a blocker appears, fall back to importing `spring-boot-dependencies` as a platform BOM and record the decision in an ADR.
- The properties-migrator is a temporary aid: enable it for one branch, capture its output in the PR discussion, then remove it before merge.

## Notice on labels

No dedicated `chore` or `dependencies` label exists in this repository. `enhancement` is the closest available umbrella; combined with `backend` and `size:L` it reflects both the area and the scope. Introducing a `chore` label is a repo-hygiene decision for the maintainer and out of scope here.

## Beschreibung

Die gesamte Projektdokumentation soll ins Deutsche übersetzt werden, um die Zugänglichkeit für deutschsprachige Beitragende zu verbessern.

- `README.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `CLA.md`
- Alle Dateien in `docs/` (ADRs, Features, Discussions, Design)

opened_issues.title: chore(frontend): bump all frontend dependencies to latest stable (MUI 9, Vite 8, TypeScript 6, ESLint 10)
opened_issues.author: criew
opened_issues.body:
## Summary

Upgrade every frontend dependency in `frontend/package.json` to its latest stable release. Includes the major bumps MUI v7 → v9, Vite 7 → 8, TypeScript 5.9 → 6.0, ESLint 9 → 10, and `react-router-dom` 7 → `react-router` 8, plus a long tail of patch/minor bumps.

## Motivation

- Keep the frontend on a supported baseline; several majors have shipped since the last bump.
- **ESLint v9 reaches end-of-life on 2026-08-06.** After that we would run on an unsupported linter — this alone makes the upgrade time-critical (window of days, not weeks).
- MUI v9 (2026-04-07) is the current stable line — v8 was intentionally skipped by the MUI team to align with MUI X v9, and staying on v7 pushes us further away from bug fixes and the promised sx-prop performance wins.
- Vite 8 (2026-03-12) replaces esbuild+Rollup with Rolldown (Rust), yielding 5–30× build speedups — big local and CI DX win.
- TypeScript 6 (2026-03-23) makes strict mode the default and removes ES5 target and other deprecated features; catching up now is cheaper than after TS 7 (Go-based) lands.
- Consolidating patch/minor bumps in the same PR keeps the churn contained and CI baselines stable.

## Scope

Frontend-only. All version changes go through `frontend/package.json` + `package-lock.json`.

| Package | Current | Target |
|---|---|---|
| react | 19.2.0 | 19.2.8 |
| react-dom | 19.2.0 | 19.2.8 |
| @mui/material | 7.3.8 | 9.x (latest patch) |
| @mui/icons-material | 7.3.8 | 9.x (latest patch) |
| @emotion/react / @emotion/styled | current | latest patch compatible with MUI 9 |
| vite | 7.3.1 | 8.0.x |
| @vitejs/plugin-react | current | latest compatible with Vite 8 |
| vitest | 4.0.18 | latest 4.x patch (v5 remains Beta, out of scope) |
| typescript | 5.9.3 | 6.0.x |
| typescript-eslint | 8.48.0 | 8.65.x (TS 6 support prerequisite) |
| eslint | 9.39.1 | 10.0.x |
| react-router-dom | 7.13.0 | remove; migrate to `react-router` 8.x (+ `react-router/dom` subpath) |
| zustand | 5.0.11 | 5.0.14 |
| msw | 2.12.10 | 2.14.x |
| axios | 1.13.5 | 1.19.0 |
| oidc-client-ts | 3.4.1 | 3.5.0 |
| @testing-library/react | 16.3.2 | 16.3.2 (already latest) |
| openapi-typescript | 7.13.0 | 7.13.0 (already latest) |
| Any transitive dev tooling (Prettier, @types/*, plugins) | — | bump patches together |

## Out of Scope

- Backend dependency bumps — tracked separately.
- Vitest 5 (still Beta as of 2026-08-01).
- TypeScript 7 (still RC, Go-based rewrite).
- React 20 (does not exist).
- New product features; this is a pure infrastructure/chore bump.

## Migration Steps

Ordered so the shortest-fuse items land first, then risk-heavy majors:

1. **ESLint 10 + typescript-eslint 8.65** — urgent (v9 EOL 2026-08-06). Only breaking change is the removal of legacy `.eslintrc.*`; OPAA already uses flat config, so risk is minimal. Verify `npm run lint` stays green.
2. **TypeScript 6.0.x** — expect fallout from `strict: true` becoming the default. Two-step plan: (a) bump TS + typescript-eslint and record diagnostics; (b) fix or temporarily narrow strict flags if the churn is too large for one PR, and document the deferred cleanup as follow-up issues. Remove any ES5-target references from `tsconfig*.json`.
3. **Vite 8 + `@vitejs/plugin-react`** — Rolldown replaces esbuild+Rollup. Rename `build.rollupOptions` → `build.rolldownOptions` and `optimizeDeps.esbuildOptions` → `optimizeDeps.rolldownOptions`. Re-check CJS-interop of any legacy dependencies. Confirm Node 20+ everywhere (local, CI, Docker images).
4. **MUI v7 → v9** — component refactors: remove `direction="column"` / `direction="column-reverse"` usages from `Stack`/etc. (feature removed), swap any deprecated `*Outline` icons, drop deprecated Accordion `TransitionComponent`/`TransitionProps` and removed AccordionSummary classes, adopt the new `nativeButton` prop on `ButtonBase` where relevant. Rerun the app and audit for visual regressions.
5. **`react-router-dom` → `react-router` 8** — v8 removes the `react-router-dom` package entirely. Migrate imports to `react-router` and `react-router/dom`; verify ESM-only builds still play with our Vite config; opt in/out of default-on middleware deliberately.
6. **Vitest** — bump to the latest 4.x patch (no major).
7. **Long tail** — bump Axios 1.19 (see breaking-change list below), Zustand 5.0.14, MSW 2.14.x, oidc-client-ts 3.5.0, openapi-typescript patch if any, `@testing-library/react` patch if any, React/React-DOM patch to 19.2.8, plus Emotion, Fontsource, and other transitive dev tooling.
8. **Verify.** Run the full pre-push checklist: `npm run format:check`, `npm run lint`, `npm run test`, `npm run build`; then `VITE_ENABLE_MOCKS=true npm run dev` and click through the main flows to confirm nothing regressed.

## Breaking Changes to Watch

**ESLint 10** — legacy `.eslintrc.*` removed (OPAA is already on flat config). Release notes: https://eslint.org/blog/2026/02/eslint-v10.0.0-released/

**typescript-eslint 8.65** — TS 6 support is still landing (tracking issue #12123, opened 2026-03-10); currently declares `>=4.8.4 <6.1.0`. Verify the peer range matches the TS 6 patch we adopt. Releases: https://github.com/typescript-eslint/typescript-eslint/releases

**TypeScript 6.0** — strict mode default; ES5 target removed; several deprecated features gone (prepend projects, `out` compilation, namespace-module augmentation). Blog: https://devblogs.microsoft.com/typescript/announcing-typescript-6-0/

**Vite 8** — Rolldown backend, Node 20+ required, `rollupOptions`/`esbuildOptions` renamed, CJS-interop tightened. Blog: https://vite.dev/blog/announcing-vite8 · Migration: https://vite.dev/guide/migration

**MUI v9 (skipping v8)** — `direction` prop no longer accepts `column`/`column-reverse`; legacy `*Outline` icons removed; Accordion `TransitionComponent`/`TransitionProps` and specific AccordionSummary classes removed; new `nativeButton` prop for `ButtonBase`; up to 30% sx-prop perf improvement. Announcement: https://mui.com/blog/introducing-mui-v9/

**react-router 8** — `react-router-dom` package removed; import paths change to `react-router` + `react-router/dom`; ESM-only; middleware on by default. The v7 team frames v8 as "non-breaking" but the package rename is effectively a breaking change for us. Blog: https://remix.run/blog/react-router-v8 · Upgrade v7 → v8: https://reactrouter.com/upgrading/v7 · Changelog: https://reactrouter.com/changelog

**Axios 1.19** — several behavior changes despite minor semver:
- URL params are percent-encoded by default.
- Stricter HTTP/HTTPS URL validation (requires `//` after protocol).
- New `allowAbsoluteUrls` config; URL combination logic changed.
- Merged config/header objects use null-prototype.
- Fetch adapter enforces `maxBodyLength` / `maxContentLength`.
- Sync interceptor error stops further request interceptors.
- Upgrade guide: https://axios.rest/pages/getting-started/upgrade-guide

**MSW 2.14.x**, **Zustand 5.0.14**, **oidc-client-ts 3.5.0**, **React 19.2.8** — patch/minor releases, no expected breaking changes. Zustand migration reference: https://zustand.docs.pmnd.rs/reference/migrations/migrating-to-v5

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All frontend versions in `frontend/package.json` updated per the Scope table (or with a documented reason for any skip).
- [ ] `npm ci` clean install succeeds.
- [ ] `npm run format:check` passes.
- [ ] `npm run lint` passes on ESLint 10 flat config.
- [ ] `npm run test` (Vitest) green.
- [ ] `npm run build` produces a working production bundle.
- [ ] `VITE_ENABLE_MOCKS=true npm run dev` starts and the main flows (login, workspace, chat) work without regressions.
- [ ] No deprecation warnings in the console/build logs from the bumped packages (or each remaining one is triaged in the PR body).
- [ ] `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `README.md`, and `docs/decisions/0002-mvp-technology-stack.md` version references updated (React Router now `react-router`, MUI v9, Vite 8, TS 6).
- [ ] Documentation updated (standing criterion for architectural changes) — brief migration notes in the PR body; ADR draft only if a structural decision emerges (e.g. dropping `react-router-dom` compatibility shim, changing strict-mode posture).

## Dependencies

Soft dependency: recommended to land after the backend Spring Boot 4 migration issue so the two large migrations do not fight over CI. No hard blocker — could start in parallel if the branch is kept isolated.

## References

- React releases: https://github.com/facebook/react/releases
- MUI v9 announcement: https://mui.com/blog/introducing-mui-v9/
- Vite 8 announcement: https://vite.dev/blog/announcing-vite8
- Vite migration guide: https://vite.dev/guide/migration
- Vitest v4 blog: https://vitest.dev/blog/vitest-4
- TypeScript 6 announcement: https://devblogs.microsoft.com/typescript/announcing-typescript-6-0/
- react-router v8 blog: https://remix.run/blog/react-router-v8
- react-router v7 → v8 upgrade guide: https://reactrouter.com/upgrading/v7
- react-router changelog: https://reactrouter.com/changelog
- Zustand v5 migration: https://zustand.docs.pmnd.rs/reference/migrations/migrating-to-v5
- MSW blog: https://mswjs.io/blog/
- ESLint 10 release: https://eslint.org/blog/2026/02/eslint-v10.0.0-released/
- typescript-eslint releases: https://github.com/typescript-eslint/typescript-eslint/releases
- Axios upgrade guide: https://axios.rest/pages/getting-started/upgrade-guide
- openapi-typescript 8 roadmap discussion: https://github.com/openapi-ts/openapi-typescript/discussions/2559
- @testing-library/react repo: https://github.com/testing-library/react-testing-library

## Technical Notes

- Vite 8 requires Node 20+ — confirm local `.nvmrc`, CI matrix, and Docker images all satisfy this before merging.
- ESLint v9 EOL is 2026-08-06; treat step 1 as the hard-priority milestone and, if the full migration will not land in time, split ESLint 10 out into its own fast-track PR.
- MUI intentionally skipped v8 for MUI X alignment; we go v7 → v9 in one step (there is no supported v8 stop).
- typescript-eslint's TS 6 support is still stabilizing (issue #12123). If we hit peer-range warnings, pin to the newest published typescript-eslint that officially supports the exact TS 6 patch we choose.
- Vitest 5 is intentionally excluded here — reassess in a follow-up once it goes stable.

## Notice on labels

Same as the backend bump issue: no dedicated `chore` or `dependencies` label exists in this repo. `enhancement` + `frontend` + `size:L` is the closest reasonable combination. Introducing a `chore` label is a repo-hygiene decision for the maintainer and out of scope here.

Where a rewrite is disproportionate, keep the deprecated Jackson-2 module (`spring-boot-jackson2`) explicitly and document why.
5. **Spring AI 2.0 migration.** Bump `spring-ai` to 2.0.x, adjust to the JSpecify null-safety annotations and any renamed helpers referenced in the Spring AI 2.0 release notes.
6. **Property renames.** Apply the SB4 property-rename table (e.g. `spring.jackson.read/write.*` → `spring.jackson.json.read/write.*`, `spring.data.mongodb.*` → `spring.mongodb.*`, `spring.dao.exceptiontranslation.enabled` → `spring.persistence.exceptiontranslation.enabled`, `spring.session.redis.*` → `spring.session.data.redis.*`, `spring.kafka.retry.topic.backoff.random` → `spring.kafka.retry.topic.backoff.jitter`). Cross-check with the properties-migrator output.
7. **Package/type moves.** Update imports: `BootstrapRegistry` (moved to `org.springframework.boot.bootstrap`), `EnvironmentPostProcessor` (moved to `org.springframework.boot`), test-only `@PropertyMapping` (moved to `org.springframework.boot.test.context`).
8. **Actuator nullability.** Replace `org.springframework.lang.Nullable` with `org.jspecify.annotations.Nullable` in Actuator-touching code.
9. **Auto-config sanity check.** We do not use Undertow, Pulsar Reactive, Spring Session Hazelcast/MongoDB, or Spring Batch, but confirm nothing in our build depends on them. Verify DevTools live-reload (now off by default) and Health Probes (now on by default) still match our expectations.
10. **Adjacent bumps.** Bump Spotless (8.9.0), OpenAPI Generator (7.23.0), JJWT (0.13.0), Caffeine (3.2.4), and re-run generation for OpenAPI DTOs; confirm the generator's Spring template still emits code that compiles against SB4 (esp. `useSpringBoot3` flag semantics).
11. **Gradle wrapper.** `./gradlew wrapper --gradle-version 9.6 --distribution-type all` and commit both `gradle-wrapper.properties` and `gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.jar`.
12. **Verify.** `./gradlew clean spotlessCheck build test` green; `./gradlew bootRun` boots against the local Docker Compose stack; Actuator health endpoint responds; OpenAPI-generated DTOs still round-trip via the frontend contract.

## Breaking Changes to Watch

Sourced from the official Spring Boot 4.0 Migration Guide and 4.0 / 4.1 release notes:

1. **Jackson 3 becomes the default** (group id `tools.jackson`). Renamed annotations and helpers (`@JsonComponent` → `@JacksonComponent`, `@JsonMixin` → `@JacksonMixin`, `JsonObjectSerializer` → `ObjectValueSerializer`, `Jackson2ObjectMapperBuilderCustomizer` → `JsonMapperBuilderCustomizer`); prefer `JsonMapper`/`XmlMapper` beans. Jackson-2 compatibility available via the deprecated `spring-boot-jackson2` module.
2. **Configuration property renames** — see step 6 above.
3. **Package/type moves** — see step 7 above.
4. **Auto-configuration removals**: Undertow (not Servlet-6.1-compatible), Pulsar Reactive, Spring Session Hazelcast/MongoDB, Spock integration. DevTools live-reload defaults to off; Actuator health probes (liveness/readiness) default to on.
5. **Actuator nullability annotations** switched from Spring's `Nullable` to JSpecify `Nullable`.
6. **Spring Data changes**: Elasticsearch `RestClient` → `Rest5Client` (`Rest5ClientBuilderCustomizer`); MongoDB UUID/BigDecimal representation now requires explicit configuration.
7. **Spring Batch** runs in-memory by default; DB-backed storage needs the new `spring-boot-starter-batch-jdbc`.
8. **Removed from dependency management**: Spring Retry (moved to Spring Framework), classic uber-jar loader, embedded exec launch scripts, Undertow.

Additional watch items:

- Spring AI 2.0 targets Spring Framework 7 / SB4 / Jackson 3 / JSpecify — 1.1.x has no forward-compat guarantee (see the compat discussion linked below).
- OpenAPI Generator 7.23+ contains breaking changes with fallback flags; re-check the generated DTO diff.
- Liquibase 5.x and Testcontainers 2.x are major bumps managed via the SB4 BOM — read their changelogs before merging.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All backend versions in `backend/gradle/libs.versions.toml` updated per the Scope table (or with a documented reason if a target release regresses).
- [ ] `./gradlew clean spotlessCheck build test` passes locally.
- [ ] `./gradlew bootRun` starts against the local Docker Compose stack; `/actuator/health` returns 200.
- [ ] All SB4 property renames applied (or explicitly acknowledged via the `spring-boot-properties-migrator` output) in every `application*.yml`.
- [ ] Jackson usages migrated to the SB4/Jackson 3 idioms (or explicitly kept on the `spring-boot-jackson2` shim with a code comment).
- [ ] Gradle wrapper on 9.6, wrapper jar committed.
- [ ] `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, and `docs/decisions/0002-mvp-technology-stack.md` version references updated to match the new baseline.
- [ ] Documentation updated (standing criterion for architectural changes) — release-notes-style summary in the PR body plus a follow-up ADR draft if any structural decision emerged (e.g. Jackson 3 adoption strategy, whether to keep the dependency-management plugin).

## Dependencies

None. Can start as soon as it is prioritized. Recommendation: merge this before the frontend bump issue so the two migrations do not overlap in CI red time.

## References

- Spring Boot 4.0 Release Notes: https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/wiki/Spring-Boot-4.0-Release-Notes
- Spring Boot 4.1 Release Notes: https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/wiki/Spring-Boot-4.1-Release-Notes
- Spring Boot 4.0 Migration Guide: https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/wiki/Spring-Boot-4.0-Migration-Guide
- Spring Boot 4.0 GA announcement: https://spring.io/blog/2025/11/20/spring-boot-4-0-0-available-now/
- Spring Boot 4.1 GA announcement: https://spring.io/blog/2026/06/10/spring-boot-4/
- Spring AI 2.0 GA announcement: https://spring.io/blog/2026/06/12/spring-ai-2-0-0-GA-available-now/
- Spring AI Boot 4 compatibility discussion: https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-ai/discussions/5149
- Spring Boot dependency management plugin docs: https://docs.spring.io/spring-boot/gradle-plugin/managing-dependencies.html
- Spotless changelog: https://github.com/diffplug/spotless/blob/main/plugin-gradle/CHANGES.md
- OpenAPI Generator releases: https://github.com/OpenAPITools/openapi-generator/releases
- Liquibase releases: https://github.com/liquibase/liquibase/releases
- Testcontainers Java releases: https://github.com/testcontainers/testcontainers-java/releases
- JJWT changelog: https://github.com/jwtk/jjwt/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
- Caffeine: https://github.com/ben-manes/caffeine

## Technical Notes

- Java 21 is already at or above the SB4 baseline (SB4 requires 17+); no JDK bump needed for the runtime.
- Gradle 9.3.1 is above the SB4 minimum (8.14+); bump to 9.6 is quality-of-life, not required.
- GraalVM native-image support would require Java 25+ — out of scope, but worth capturing as a future consideration.
- The Spring Dependency Management plugin is still compatible with SB4 for now. If a blocker appears, fall back to importing `spring-boot-dependencies` as a platform BOM and record the decision in an ADR.
- The properties-migrator is a temporary aid: enable it for one branch, capture its output in the PR discussion, then remove it before merge.

## Notice on labels

No dedicated `chore` or `dependencies` label exists in this repository. `enhancement` is the closest available umbrella; combined with `backend` and `size:L` it reflects both the area and the scope. Introducing a `chore` label is a repo-hygiene decision for the maintainer and out of scope here.

## Zusammenfassung

Coordinated upgrade of the backend to **Spring Boot 4.1.0** and **Spring AI 2.0.0**, plus the supporting library and tooling bumps. Backend-only; no product behavior changes.

### Versions

All version changes go through `backend/gradle/libs.versions.toml`.

| Library / Tool | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Spring Boot | 3.5.10 | 4.1.0 |
| Spring AI | 1.1.2 | 2.0.0 |
| Spring Dependency Management plugin | 1.1.7 | 1.1.7 (unchanged, SB4-compatible) |
| Spotless | 8.2.1 | 8.9.0 |
| OpenAPI Generator | 7.20.0 | 7.24.0 |
| JJWT | 0.12.6 | 0.13.0 |
| Caffeine | 3.2.0 | 3.2.4 |
| Awaitility | 4.3.0 (pinned) | managed by SB4 BOM |
| Liquibase | 4.x (SB3.5 BOM) | 5.0.3 (SB4 BOM) |
| Testcontainers | 1.x (SB3.5 BOM) | 2.0.5 (SB4 BOM) |
| Gradle wrapper | 9.3.1 | 9.6.1 |
| Java | 21 | 21 (unchanged) |

Gradle 9.6.1 is the latest 9.6 patch; the issue asked for "9.6". Spring Boot 4.1.0 is the current 4.1 release — no 4.1.x patch exists yet.

### Breaking changes handled

**Spring Boot 4 package and module moves**
- `org.springframework.boot.actuate.health.{Health,HealthIndicator,Status}` → `org.springframework.boot.health.contributor.*`
- `org.springframework.boot.web.client.RestClientCustomizer` → `org.springframework.boot.restclient.RestClientCustomizer`
- Test slices are separate starters now: `spring-boot-starter-webmvc-test` (`@WebMvcTest` → `org.springframework.boot.webmvc.test.autoconfigure`), `spring-boot-starter-data-jpa-test` (`@DataJpaTest` → `org.springframework.boot.data.jpa.test.autoconfigure`), and `spring-boot-starter-security-test` (replaces the bare `spring-security-test` dependency — without it the `@WebMvcTest` slice has no `HttpSecurity` bean).
- Liquibase auto-configuration moved out of `spring-boot-autoconfigure`; `liquibase-core` was replaced with `spring-boot-starter-liquibase`. Without this, Liquibase silently never runs.

**Jackson 3 (default in SB4)**
- The auto-configured bean is `tools.jackson.databind.json.JsonMapper`, not `ObjectMapper`. `RateLimitConfiguration` / `RateLimitFilter` were migrated. The `spring-boot-jackson2` shim is deliberately **not** used — rationale in [ADR-0007](docs/decisions/0007-jackson-3-adoption.md).
- The OpenAPI-generated DTOs need no change: Jackson 3 still reads `com.fasterxml.jackson.annotation.*`.

**Spring AI 2.0**
- `spring-ai-advisors-vector-store` renamed to `spring-ai-vector-store-advisor`.
- `TokenTextSplitter`'s 5-arg constructor is gone; switched to the builder.
- Property renames (confirmed via `spring-boot-properties-migrator`, then removed again): `spring.ai.{openai,ollama}.{chat,embedding}.options.*` → `…​.{chat,embedding}.*`, and `maxTokens` → `max-tokens`. Environment variable names are unchanged, so `.env` files and `docs/deployment.md` need no update.
- `ChatModel.getOptions()` is now merged into every request. Bare Mockito mocks return `null` there, so `AnswerGenerationServiceTest` and `QueryIntegrationTest` now stub it.

**Testcontainers 2**
- All module artifacts gained a `testcontainers-` prefix (`org.testcontainers:postgresql` → `org.testcontainers:testcontainers-postgresql`, etc.).
- `PostgreSQLContainer` moved to `org.testcontainers.postgresql` and is no longer generic (`PostgreSQLContainer<?>` → `PostgreSQLContainer`).

**Checked, no action needed**
- No `javax.*` leftovers requiring migration (only `javax.crypto` / `javax.net.ssl`, which are JDK packages).
- No `org.springframework.lang.Nullable` in hand-written code. The generated DTOs still emit it (generator-side; warning only).
- No Undertow, Pulsar Reactive, Spring Session Hazelcast/MongoDB, Spring Batch, Spring Retry, Elasticsearch or MongoDB usage.
- No Spring Boot core property renames were reported by the migrator.
- Health probes (liveness/readiness) are on by default in SB4 and now appear under `/actuator/health` — both return 200.
- OpenAPI Generator 7.24 emits some extra Jackson annotations (`@JsonProperty` on accessors, class-level `@JsonInclude(NON_NULL)`, `@JsonSetter(nulls = SKIP)`) and drops one redundant field-level `@Valid` where the getter still carries it. No contract or validation change; the DTO diff against 7.20 was reviewed.

### Verification

- `./gradlew clean spotlessCheck build test` — green (backend).
- `./gradlew bootRun` against the Docker Compose Postgres — starts, Liquibase 5 applies all 8 changesets to a fresh database, `/actuator/health` returns 200 `UP`, `/actuator/health/{liveness,readiness}` return 200.
- Frontend `format:check`, `lint`, `build`, `test` (122 tests) — green, unchanged by this PR.
- No deprecation warnings remain in hand-written code.

opened.title: chore(frontend): bump all frontend dependencies to latest stable (MUI 9, Vite 8, TypeScript 6, ESLint 10)
opened.author: criew
opened.body:
## Summary

Upgrade every frontend dependency in `frontend/package.json` to its latest stable release. Includes the major bumps MUI v7 → v9, Vite 7 → 8, TypeScript 5.9 → 6.0, ESLint 9 → 10, and `react-router-dom` 7 → `react-router` 8, plus a long tail of patch/minor bumps.

## Motivation

- Keep the frontend on a supported baseline; several majors have shipped since the last bump.
- **ESLint v9 reaches end-of-life on 2026-08-06.** After that we would run on an unsupported linter — this alone makes the upgrade time-critical (window of days, not weeks).
- MUI v9 (2026-04-07) is the current stable line — v8 was intentionally skipped by the MUI team to align with MUI X v9, and staying on v7 pushes us further away from bug fixes and the promised sx-prop performance wins.
- Vite 8 (2026-03-12) replaces esbuild+Rollup with Rolldown (Rust), yielding 5–30× build speedups — big local and CI DX win.
- TypeScript 6 (2026-03-23) makes strict mode the default and removes ES5 target and other deprecated features; catching up now is cheaper than after TS 7 (Go-based) lands.
- Consolidating patch/minor bumps in the same PR keeps the churn contained and CI baselines stable.

## Scope

Frontend-only. All version changes go through `frontend/package.json` + `package-lock.json`.

| Package | Current | Target |
|---|---|---|
| react | 19.2.0 | 19.2.8 |
| react-dom | 19.2.0 | 19.2.8 |
| @mui/material | 7.3.8 | 9.x (latest patch) |
| @mui/icons-material | 7.3.8 | 9.x (latest patch) |
| @emotion/react / @emotion/styled | current | latest patch compatible with MUI 9 |
| vite | 7.3.1 | 8.0.x |
| @vitejs/plugin-react | current | latest compatible with Vite 8 |
| vitest | 4.0.18 | latest 4.x patch (v5 remains Beta, out of scope) |
| typescript | 5.9.3 | 6.0.x |
| typescript-eslint | 8.48.0 | 8.65.x (TS 6 support prerequisite) |
| eslint | 9.39.1 | 10.0.x |
| react-router-dom | 7.13.0 | remove; migrate to `react-router` 8.x (+ `react-router/dom` subpath) |
| zustand | 5.0.11 | 5.0.14 |
| msw | 2.12.10 | 2.14.x |
| axios | 1.13.5 | 1.19.0 |
| oidc-client-ts | 3.4.1 | 3.5.0 |
| @testing-library/react | 16.3.2 | 16.3.2 (already latest) |
| openapi-typescript | 7.13.0 | 7.13.0 (already latest) |
| Any transitive dev tooling (Prettier, @types/*, plugins) | — | bump patches together |

## Out of Scope

- Backend dependency bumps — tracked separately.
- Vitest 5 (still Beta as of 2026-08-01).
- TypeScript 7 (still RC, Go-based rewrite).
- React 20 (does not exist).
- New product features; this is a pure infrastructure/chore bump.

## Migration Steps

Ordered so the shortest-fuse items land first, then risk-heavy majors:

1. **ESLint 10 + typescript-eslint 8.65** — urgent (v9 EOL 2026-08-06). Only breaking change is the removal of legacy `.eslintrc.*`; OPAA already uses flat config, so risk is minimal. Verify `npm run lint` stays green.
2. **TypeScript 6.0.x** — expect fallout from `strict: true` becoming the default. Two-step plan: (a) bump TS + typescript-eslint and record diagnostics; (b) fix or temporarily narrow strict flags if the churn is too large for one PR, and document the deferred cleanup as follow-up issues. Remove any ES5-target references from `tsconfig*.json`.
3. **Vite 8 + `@vitejs/plugin-react`** — Rolldown replaces esbuild+Rollup. Rename `build.rollupOptions` → `build.rolldownOptions` and `optimizeDeps.esbuildOptions` → `optimizeDeps.rolldownOptions`. Re-check CJS-interop of any legacy dependencies. Confirm Node 20+ everywhere (local, CI, Docker images).
4. **MUI v7 → v9** — component refactors: remove `direction="column"` / `direction="column-reverse"` usages from `Stack`/etc. (feature removed), swap any deprecated `*Outline` icons, drop deprecated Accordion `TransitionComponent`/`TransitionProps` and removed AccordionSummary classes, adopt the new `nativeButton` prop on `ButtonBase` where relevant. Rerun the app and audit for visual regressions.
5. **`react-router-dom` → `react-router` 8** — v8 removes the `react-router-dom` package entirely. Migrate imports to `react-router` and `react-router/dom`; verify ESM-only builds still play with our Vite config; opt in/out of default-on middleware deliberately.
6. **Vitest** — bump to the latest 4.x patch (no major).
7. **Long tail** — bump Axios 1.19 (see breaking-change list below), Zustand 5.0.14, MSW 2.14.x, oidc-client-ts 3.5.0, openapi-typescript patch if any, `@testing-library/react` patch if any, React/React-DOM patch to 19.2.8, plus Emotion, Fontsource, and other transitive dev tooling.
8. **Verify.** Run the full pre-push checklist: `npm run format:check`, `npm run lint`, `npm run test`, `npm run build`; then `VITE_ENABLE_MOCKS=true npm run dev` and click through the main flows to confirm nothing regressed.

## Breaking Changes to Watch

**ESLint 10** — legacy `.eslintrc.*` removed (OPAA is already on flat config). Release notes: https://eslint.org/blog/2026/02/eslint-v10.0.0-released/

**typescript-eslint 8.65** — TS 6 support is still landing (tracking issue #12123, opened 2026-03-10); currently declares `>=4.8.4 <6.1.0`. Verify the peer range matches the TS 6 patch we adopt. Releases: https://github.com/typescript-eslint/typescript-eslint/releases

**TypeScript 6.0** — strict mode default; ES5 target removed; several deprecated features gone (prepend projects, `out` compilation, namespace-module augmentation). Blog: https://devblogs.microsoft.com/typescript/announcing-typescript-6-0/

**Vite 8** — Rolldown backend, Node 20+ required, `rollupOptions`/`esbuildOptions` renamed, CJS-interop tightened. Blog: https://vite.dev/blog/announcing-vite8 · Migration: https://vite.dev/guide/migration

**MUI v9 (skipping v8)** — `direction` prop no longer accepts `column`/`column-reverse`; legacy `*Outline` icons removed; Accordion `TransitionComponent`/`TransitionProps` and specific AccordionSummary classes removed; new `nativeButton` prop for `ButtonBase`; up to 30% sx-prop perf improvement. Announcement: https://mui.com/blog/introducing-mui-v9/

**react-router 8** — `react-router-dom` package removed; import paths change to `react-router` + `react-router/dom`; ESM-only; middleware on by default. The v7 team frames v8 as "non-breaking" but the package rename is effectively a breaking change for us. Blog: https://remix.run/blog/react-router-v8 · Upgrade v7 → v8: https://reactrouter.com/upgrading/v7 · Changelog: https://reactrouter.com/changelog

**Axios 1.19** — several behavior changes despite minor semver:
- URL params are percent-encoded by default.
- Stricter HTTP/HTTPS URL validation (requires `//` after protocol).
- New `allowAbsoluteUrls` config; URL combination logic changed.
- Merged config/header objects use null-prototype.
- Fetch adapter enforces `maxBodyLength` / `maxContentLength`.
- Sync interceptor error stops further request interceptors.
- Upgrade guide: https://axios.rest/pages/getting-started/upgrade-guide

**MSW 2.14.x**, **Zustand 5.0.14**, **oidc-client-ts 3.5.0**, **React 19.2.8** — patch/minor releases, no expected breaking changes. Zustand migration reference: https://zustand.docs.pmnd.rs/reference/migrations/migrating-to-v5

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All frontend versions in `frontend/package.json` updated per the Scope table (or with a documented reason for any skip).
- [ ] `npm ci` clean install succeeds.
- [ ] `npm run format:check` passes.
- [ ] `npm run lint` passes on ESLint 10 flat config.
- [ ] `npm run test` (Vitest) green.
- [ ] `npm run build` produces a working production bundle.
- [ ] `VITE_ENABLE_MOCKS=true npm run dev` starts and the main flows (login, workspace, chat) work without regressions.
- [ ] No deprecation warnings in the console/build logs from the bumped packages (or each remaining one is triaged in the PR body).
- [ ] `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `README.md`, and `docs/decisions/0002-mvp-technology-stack.md` version references updated (React Router now `react-router`, MUI v9, Vite 8, TS 6).

- Align on the Jakarta EE 11 / Servlet 6.1 / Spring Framework 7 stack now that Java 21 is our baseline.

- Reduce carrying cost by bumping the long tail (Spotless, OpenAPI Generator, JJWT, Caffeine, Awaitility, Gradle wrapper) in the same pass.

## Scope

Backend-only dependency and tooling bumps. All version changes go through `backend/gradle/libs.versions.toml` per the repository dependency-management rules.

| Library / Tool | Current | Target |
|---|---|---|
| Spring Boot | 3.5.10 | 4.1.x (latest patch of 4.1) |
| Spring AI | 1.1.2 | 2.0.x (latest patch of 2.0) |
| Spring Dependency Management plugin | 1.1.7 | 1.1.7 (verify SB4 compatibility; keep unless a blocker) |
| Spotless | 8.2.1 | 8.9.0 |
| OpenAPI Generator | 7.20.0 | 7.23.0 (or 7.24.0 if released; keep `useSpringBoot3=true` semantics working under SB4) |
| JJWT | 0.12.6 | 0.13.0 |
| Caffeine | 3.2.0 | 3.2.4 |
| Awaitility | 4.3.0 | Latest patch pulled via SB4 BOM |
| Liquibase Core | via SB3.5 BOM (4.x) | Whatever the SB4 BOM ships (currently 5.x); confirm changelog compatibility |
| Testcontainers | via SB3.5 BOM (1.x) | Whatever the SB4 BOM ships (currently 2.x); regenerate/validate integration tests |
| Gradle Wrapper | 9.3.1 | 9.6 |
| Java baseline | 21 | 21 (no change required) |

## Out of Scope

- Frontend dependency bumps — tracked in a separate issue.
- Product/feature behavior changes; this is a pure infrastructure/chore bump.
- Removing or replacing the `spring-dependency-management` plugin with Gradle's native BOM import — evaluate but do not execute here.
- Migrating to a Jackson-3-only stack when a Jackson-2 compatibility shim (`spring-boot-jackson2`) already unblocks us; only remove Jackson 2 usages that are directly touched.
- GraalVM native-image (would require Java 25+); note but do not adopt.

## Migration Steps

1. **Land on latest 3.5.x first.** Bump to the freshest Spring Boot 3.5 patch, run `./gradlew build test`, and clean up any deprecation warnings that block a clean SB4 upgrade.
2. **Wire in the `spring-boot-properties-migrator`** dependency for the first SB4 boot to surface renamed `application.yml` properties.
3. **Upgrade the platform.** Bump `spring-boot`, `spring-boot-dependencies`, and the Spring Boot Gradle plugin to 4.1.x. Confirm Spring Framework 7 + Jakarta EE 11 assumptions in our code (Servlet 6.1 signatures, no `javax.*` leftovers).
4. **Jackson 3 alignment.** Replace usages of `@JsonComponent` → `@JacksonComponent`, `@JsonMixin` → `@JacksonMixin`, `JsonObjectSerializer` → `ObjectValueSerializer`, `Jackson2ObjectMapperBuilderCustomizer` → `JsonMapperBuilderCustomizer`; move `ObjectMapper` bean expectations to `JsonMapper` / `XmlMapper` where applicable. 5. **Spring AI 2.0 migration.** Bump `spring-ai` to 2.0.x, adjust to the JSpecify null-safety annotations and any renamed helpers referenced in the Spring AI 2.0 release notes.
6. **Property renames.** Apply the SB4 property-rename table (e.g. `spring.jackson.read/write.*` → `spring.jackson.json.read/write.*`, `spring.data.mongodb.*` → `spring.mongodb.*`, `spring.dao.exceptiontranslation.enabled` → `spring.persistence.exceptiontranslation.enabled`, `spring.session.redis.*` → `spring.session.data.redis.*`, `spring.kafka.retry.topic.backoff.random` → `spring.kafka.retry.topic.backoff.jitter`). 9. **Auto-config sanity check.** We do not use Undertow, Pulsar Reactive, Spring Session Hazelcast/MongoDB, or Spring Batch, but confirm nothing in our build depends on them. Verify DevTools live-reload (now off by default) and Health Probes (now on by default) still match our expectations.

3. **Package/type moves** — see step 7 above.

None. Can start as soon as it is prioritized. Recommendation: merge this before the frontend bump issue so the two migrations do not overlap in CI red time.

- Spring Boot 4.1 Release Notes: https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/wiki/Spring-Boot-4.1-Release-Notes
- Spring Boot 4.0 Migration Guide: https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/wiki/Spring-Boot-4.0-Migration-Guide
- Spring Boot 4.0 GA announcement: https://spring.io/blog/2025/11/20/spring-boot-4-0-0-available-now/
- Spring Boot 4.1 GA announcement: https://spring.io/blog/2026/06/10/spring-boot-4/
- Spring AI 2.0 GA announcement: https://spring.io/blog/2026/06/12/spring-ai-2-0-0-GA-available-now/
- Spring AI Boot 4 compatibility discussion: https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-ai/discussions/5149
- Spring Boot dependency management plugin docs: https://docs.spring.io/spring-boot/gradle-plugin/managing-dependencies.html
- Spotless changelog: https://github.com/diffplug/spotless/blob/main/plugin-gradle/CHANGES.md
- OpenAPI Generator releases: https://github.com/OpenAPITools/openapi-generator/releases

Coordinated upgrade of the backend to **Spring Boot 4.1.0** and **Spring AI 2.0.0**, plus the supporting library and tooling bumps. Backend-only; no product behavior changes.

### Versions

All version changes go through `backend/gradle/libs.versions.toml`.

| Library / Tool | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Spring Boot | 3.5.10 | 4.1.0 |
| Spring AI | 1.1.2 | 2.0.0 |
| Spring Dependency Management plugin | 1.1.7 | 1.1.7 (unchanged, SB4-compatible) |
| Spotless | 8.2.1 | 8.9.0 |
| OpenAPI Generator | 7.20.0 | 7.24.0 |
| JJWT | 0.12.6 | 0.13.0 |
| Caffeine | 3.2.0 | 3.2.4 |
| Awaitility | 4.3.0 (pinned) | managed by SB4 BOM |
| Liquibase | 4.x (SB3.5 BOM) | 5.0.3 (SB4 BOM) |
| Testcontainers | 1.x (SB3.5 BOM) | 2.0.5 (SB4 BOM) |
| Gradle wrapper | 9.3.1 | 9.6.1 |
| Java | 21 | 21 (unchanged) |

Gradle 9.6.1 is the latest 9.6 patch; the issue asked for "9.6". Spring Boot 4.1.0 is the current 4.1 release — no 4.1.x patch exists yet.

### Breaking changes handled

**Spring Boot 4 package and module moves**
- `org.springframework.boot.actuate.health.{Health,HealthIndicator,Status}` → `org.springframework.boot.health.contributor.*`
- `org.springframework.boot.web.client.RestClientCustomizer` → `org.springframework.boot.restclient.RestClientCustomizer`
- Test slices are separate starters now: `spring-boot-starter-webmvc-test` (`@WebMvcTest` → `org.springframework.boot.webmvc.test.autoconfigure`), `spring-boot-starter-data-jpa-test` (`@DataJpaTest` → `org.springframework.boot.data.jpa.test.autoconfigure`), and `spring-boot-starter-security-test` (replaces the bare `spring-security-test` dependency — without it the `@WebMvcTest` slice has no `HttpSecurity` bean).
- Liquibase auto-configuration moved out of `spring-boot-autoconfigure`; `liquibase-core` was replaced with `spring-boot-starter-liquibase`. Without this, Liquibase silently never runs.

**Jackson 3 (default in SB4)**
- The auto-configured bean is `tools.jackson.databind.json.JsonMapper`, not `ObjectMapper`. `RateLimitConfiguration` / `RateLimitFilter` were migrated. The `spring-boot-jackson2` shim is deliberately **not** used — rationale in [ADR-0007](docs/decisions/0007-jackson-3-adoption.md).
- The OpenAPI-generated DTOs need no change: Jackson 3 still reads `com.fasterxml.jackson.annotation.*`.

**Spring AI 2.0**
- `spring-ai-advisors-vector-store` renamed to `spring-ai-vector-store-advisor`.
- `TokenTextSplitter`'s 5-arg constructor is gone; switched to the builder.
- Property renames (confirmed via `spring-boot-properties-migrator`, then removed again): `spring.ai.{openai,ollama}.{chat,embedding}.options.*` → `…​.{chat,embedding}.*`, and `maxTokens` → `max-tokens`. Environment variable names are unchanged, so `.env` files and `docs/deployment.md` need no update.
- `ChatModel.getOptions()` is now merged into every request. Bare Mockito mocks return `null` there, so `AnswerGenerationServiceTest` and `QueryIntegrationTest` now stub it.

**Testcontainers 2**
- All module artifacts gained a `testcontainers-` prefix (`org.testcontainers:postgresql` → `org.testcontainers:testcontainers-postgresql`, etc.).
- `PostgreSQLContainer` moved to `org.testcontainers.postgresql` and is no longer generic (`PostgreSQLContainer<?>` → `PostgreSQLContainer`).

**Checked, no action needed**
- No `javax.*` leftovers requiring migration (only `javax.crypto` / `javax.net.ssl`, which are JDK packages).
- No `org.springframework.lang.Nullable` in hand-written code. The generated DTOs still emit it (generator-side; warning only).
- No Undertow, Pulsar Reactive, Spring Session Hazelcast/MongoDB, Spring Batch, Spring Retry, Elasticsearch or MongoDB usage.
- No Spring Boot core property renames were reported by the migrator.
- Health probes (liveness/readiness) are on by default in SB4 and now appear under `/actuator/health` — both return 200.
- OpenAPI Generator 7.24 emits some extra Jackson annotations (`@JsonProperty` on accessors, class-level `@JsonInclude(NON_NULL)`, `@JsonSetter(nulls = SKIP)`) and drops one redundant field-level `@Valid` where the getter still carries it. No contract or validation change; the DTO diff against 7.20 was reviewed.

### Verification

- `./gradlew clean spotlessCheck build test` — green (backend).
- `./gradlew bootRun` against the Docker Compose Postgres — starts, Liquibase 5 applies all 8 changesets to a fresh database, `/actuator/health` returns 200 `UP`, `/actuator/health/{liveness,readiness}` return 200.
- Frontend `format:check`, `lint`, `build`, `test` (122 tests) — green, unchanged by this PR.
- No deprecation warnings remain in hand-written code.
